page.layout: One page of running text in a single column; running head at top, page number at top right, signature at bottom left, catchword at bottom right. No margin notes.

main_text.p: ut quorundam conjuratio ejus vitam petiiffet, nisi ma-turè innotuiffet. Hos conjuratos non solum sustulit Rex, sed etiam in auctores severius inquisivit & ani-madvertit.

Abhinc rebus suis consulens, ut minaces inter Ju-dæos refrænaret, consilium cepit de munimentis condendis, quibus tales coerceat. Ante omnia Samariam condi jussit, eique nomen Sebaste destinavit, in memoriam nominis Augusti, quod hoc anno Cæsari datum fuit.
main_text.head: §. 6. Anno P. J. 4788. U. C. 728. Augusto VIII & T. Statilio Tauro II coff. Jul. 20. Herodis [?]
main_text.p: Augustus, Narbone in Galliâ Tarraconem in Hispaniâ profectus, arma ipse adversus Cantabros movit. Ægypti in præfecturâ loco Cornelii Galli, primi in eâ provinciâ Cæsaris nomine Procuratoris, fuit Ælius Gallus (an Largus?) ad bellum Arabicum missus.

Post primum actiada, qui ludus anni præcedentis autumno videtur habitus, Damasceni ad Varronem Syriæ Præsidem, sicuti ille ad Cæsarem per literas, querelas miserant contra Zenodorum, latrones excurrere in fines Damascenos clanculum facientem; ille enim Lysaniæ ditionem conduxerat: rescripsit autem Cæsar Varroni expugnanda esse latronum receptacula, atque ditionem illam regno Herodis esse adjiciendam; atque ita Tra-chon, Batanæa & Auranitis regno Herodis accesserunt.
main_text.head: §. 7. Anno P. J. 4689. U. C. 729. Augusto IX M. Junio Silano coff. Jul. 21. Herodis [?]
main_text.p: Ælius expeditionem contra Arabes suscipiens, quingentos ex Herodis satellitio suscepit auxiliares, quos cum exercitu ad mare rubrum duxit: cujus expeditionis æque apud Strabonem ac Josephum fit mentio. Circa anni medium Petronius, bellum contra Æthiopes ge-

page.notes: The chronology lines under §. 6 and §. 7 carry small superscript figures beside "Herodis" (apparently 13 11 / 15 13 and 15 11 / 16 13); these are too small and faint to read with certainty and are marked [?]. The initial "A" of "Augustus" is a decorative capital and is joined to the word. Words broken at line ends keep their printed hyphen. Catchword "rens," and signature "Gg 3" are at the foot. Italic words are judged from the scan and may be imprecise where the type is faint.
